function_question: How does nature grip smooth surfaces?

opening.text: There was a boy called Toby who had a bright red kite and a long, windy garden.
After school, Toby raced across the grass and let his kite climb higher and higher into the sky.
The wind dropped, and the kite slid under the garden shed: 60 cm back, in a gap only 5 cm high. Every stick Toby tried just pushed it further in!

card.place: A tiny gap under the garden shed
card.problem: The kite is stuck 60 cm back
card.goal: Grab it, pull it out, let it go
card.rules: Fit a gap only 5 cm high

chapters.label: Chapter 1
chapters.title: The kite under the shed
chapters.line: Toby lies flat on the grass and peers into the dark gap. His kite is right there, just out of reach.

chapters.label: Chapter 2
chapters.title: Toby asks for help
chapters.line: Sticks push, but they can't pull. Toby needs a teammate. What about you?

chapters.label: Chapter 3
chapters.title: The masters of grip
chapters.line: You and Toby meet animals that can hold on to almost anything.

chapters.label: Chapter 4
chapters.title: The secret of a good grip
chapters.line: The grip heroes share the secret they all use.

chapters.label: Chapter 5
chapters.title: Training in the grip lab
chapters.line: Toby puts a playing card on the table and lines up five tips to test.

chapters.label: Chapter 5½
chapters.title: The grip map
chapters.line: One word in the middle, and ideas branch out like a tree!

chapters.label: Chapter 6
chapters.title: The plan
chapters.line: Every great grabber starts as a drawing.

chapters.label: Chapter 7
chapters.title: The big test
chapters.line: The first try slips. You fix the tip, and try again.

chapters.label: Chapter 8
chapters.title: The kite flies again
chapters.line: Out comes the kite, and up it goes into the wind.

guide.brief: I'm Popi, your story guide. Toby's kite is stuck under the shed, and sticks only push it further in. Can you help him get it back? Let's start!
guide.your_idea: Some engineers already have a spark of an idea. Do you?
guide.nature_clues: Nature solved this millions of years ago. Tap each card to meet four nature heroes with a super grip!
guide.design_secret: Here's the secret all four heroes share…
guide.skill: Scientists predict before they test. Which tip will grip the card best?
guide.sketch: Time to draw your grabber like a real engineer!
guide.build_and_test: Build your grabber and let's see how many times out of 10 it rescues the card!
guide.retry_tip: Engineers never stop at round 1. Change ONE thing and test again!
guide.ending: And ever since then, Toby keeps YOUR grabber by the shed door. Whenever something slides into the gap, he has it back in seconds!

quick_check.question: Toby's ruler is 30 cm long. How many rulers end to end would reach the kite, 60 cm back?
quick_check.right: Right! 2 × 30 cm = 60 cm. Now the grabber needs a tip that can grip the kite and let it go.

clue_cards.name: Gecko
clue_cards.trick: Millions of tiny toe hairs that split into even tinier tips.
clue_cards.does: They touch so closely that tiny pulls add up, so it can hang from glass by one toe.

clue_cards.name: Tree frog
clue_cards.trick: Soft toe pads with a thin layer of mucus.
clue_cards.does: Grips wet leaves the way a damp finger picks up paper.

clue_cards.name: Chameleon
clue_cards.trick: A sticky, cup-shaped tip on its tongue.
clue_cards.does: Grabs an insect in a fraction of a second.

clue_cards.name: Elephant
clue_cards.trick: Finger-like parts at the tip of its trunk.
clue_cards.does: Pinches something as small as a peanut.

match_groups.label: 🦶 Touches with millions of tiny tips

predict.prompt: Grip or slip? Can each tip lift a smooth card? Predict first!
predict.explain: A hard tip only touches the card in a few tiny spots. Soft tips squish into the tiny bumps, so they touch much more of the surface and hold on.

lab.title: The grip lab
lab.predict: Which tip will lift a playing card best?

tool.name: Mind map
tool.intro: A mind map is an idea tree on paper. One big word goes in the middle, and ideas grow out from it. Today you'll use all 5 pieces.

parts.name: Centre
parts.what: Write the big question in the middle.
parts.example: 🍱 "A better lunchbox" goes in the middle.
parts.starter: In the middle I write "grip", because Toby needs to…

parts.name: Branches
parts.what: Draw lines out to the main topics.
parts.example: 🍱 Branches: keep it cold, keep it shut, easy to carry.
parts.starter: My four branches are sticky, suction, squeeze and…

parts.name: Twigs
parts.what: Add smaller ideas to each branch.
parts.example: 🍱 On "keep it cold": an ice pack, a shiny lining.
parts.starter: On the "sticky" branch I add the tree frog and…

parts.name: Pictures
parts.what: Add quick doodles so ideas pop out.
parts.example: 🍱 A tiny snowflake next to "keep it cold".

parts.name: Links
parts.what: Join ideas on different branches with a line.
parts.example: 🍱 Link "shiny lining" to "easy to carry": a light, cool bag!
parts.starter: I link two branches together, like the gecko's hairs and…

sketch_checklist: I labelled the handle, the reach and the gripping tip.
I showed how I trigger the release.

test.check_question: Try a card, a coin and a leaf. How many can it pick up?

reflection.question: Which nature trick helped your grabber grip?
